what: Campbell's makes soup and snacks. Beyond its canned soup, it owns Goldfish crackers, Pepperidge Farm, Snyder's of Hanover pretzels, Kettle chips, Prego sauces, V8 juice and the Rao's premium pasta sauce brand.
customers: Supermarkets, mass merchants, club stores and convenience chains across North America, who resell to consumers.
money: Soup, Prego sauces, Rao's, V8 and other shelf-stable meals.
Goldfish, Pepperidge Farm cookies, Snyder's pretzels, Kettle and Cape Cod chips.
moat: Campbell's condensed soup has no real substitute in the minds of its buyers, and Goldfish holds a dominant position in children's crackers. These are brands retailers must stock, which secures shelf space and allows price increases that smaller competitors cannot match.
risks: Revenue fell from $10.3B to $9.7B in the latest year shown, as shoppers moved to cheaper store brands.
Debt is about $7.5B against $394.0M of cash, much of it taken on to buy Sovos Brands and Snyder's-Lance.
The seventeen analysts average a $20.79 target, about 11% below the current $23.35 price, an unusual and meaningful bearish signal.
Snack volumes have been weak across the industry, and that is half the business.
Soup consumption has drifted down for years as eating habits shift toward fresh and prepared food.
opportunities: Free cash flow of about $678.0M against a $7.0B market value supports a long-standing dividend.
The shares trade at about 0.71 times sales and 10.3 times free cash flow.
Rao's is a genuinely premium brand growing faster than the rest of the portfolio, and premium sauce has been one of the few growing grocery categories.
Cost reduction programmes can recover margin without volume growth.
watch: Snack volume. Soup is a mature, slowly declining business that Campbell's manages for cash; the snacks half is what determines whether the company grows at all.
